title: A lift of the fibre idempotent gives the localization isomorphism
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $A\to B$ be a finite-type ring map with $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ and $C_1$ finite over $A/I$. Let $B'\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$, and let $\phi:\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ be induced by the inclusion. Suppose $B'/IB'=C'_1\times C'_2$ is a product of $A/I$-algebras whose factors map to $C_1,C_2$ respectively, and write $\varepsilon'=(1,0)\in B'/IB'$. Let $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ be an open neighbourhood of $\operatorname{Spec}(C'_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ (the subsets of primes of $B'$ that are inverse images of primes under the surjections $B'\to B'/IB'\to C'_1$, the second being the projection onto the first factor), and suppose the induced morphism $\phi^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(B')}U\to U$ is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces. Then there is $g\in B'$ whose image modulo $IB'$ is $\varepsilon'$ and whose principal open $D(g)$ is contained in $U$. For this $g$, the induced localization map $B'_g\to B_g$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex:2542-2549, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type): choose g lifting (1,0) with D(g) subset U and conclude B'_g -> B_g is an isomorphism from the homeomorphism and local-ring isomorphisms; the product step is Algebra Tag 00EE and the final local criterion is Tag 00E9

proof.text: Choose any $g_0\in B'$ whose image in $B'/IB'$ is $\varepsilon'$. Since $\varepsilon'^2=\varepsilon'$, we have $g_0(1-g_0)\in IB'$. The projection $B'/IB'\to C'_1$ is surjective with kernel $(1-\varepsilon')(B'/IB')$, so the composite $B'\to C'_1$ is surjective with kernel $K:=IB'+(1-g_0)B'$. By the correspondence between the primes of a quotient $B'/K$ and the primes of $B'$ containing $K$, the subset $\operatorname{Spec}(C'_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ of the statement is $V(K)=\{\mathfrak p:K\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$, a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ for the Zariski topology.

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2543-2546, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH ('Spec(C'_1) ... closed in Spec(B')'); the product/idempotent dictionary is Algebra Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition)

proof.text: The complement $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B')\setminus U$ is closed, so by definition of the Zariski topology $Z=V(J)$ for some ideal $J\subseteq B'$. Since $V(K)=\operatorname{Spec}(C'_1)\subseteq U$ (step 1 and the hypothesis on $U$), $V(J)\cap V(K)=\emptyset$. A prime contains $J+K$ if and only if it contains $J$ and $K$, so $V(J+K)=V(J)\cap V(K)=\emptyset$; as $V(J+K)$ is the complement of $\bigcup_{r\in J+K}D(r)$, part (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] applied to the family of all elements of $J+K$ gives $J+K=B'$. Write $1=j+k$ with $j\in J$ and $k\in K$.

source.place: Algebra Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), items (8) V(I)=emptyset iff I=R and (9)/(10) intersections of V's; used at more-algebra.tex:2543-2546 ('this is possible because Spec(C'_1) and Spec(C'_2) are disjoint and closed in Spec(B') and Spec(C'_1) is contained in U')

proof.text: Put $g=g_0j\in B'$. Then $g-g_0=-g_0k\in g_0IB'+g_0(1-g_0)B'\subseteq IB'$, because $g_0(1-g_0)\in IB'$ (step 1); so the image of $g$ in $B'/IB'$ is $\varepsilon'$. Moreover $g\in J$, so every prime of $Z=V(J)$ contains $g$, i.e. $D(g)\cap Z=\emptyset$, i.e. $D(g)\subseteq U$. This proves the first assertion.

proof.text: Let $\iota:B'\to B$ be the inclusion, so $\phi=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$, whose map on global sections is $\iota$ under $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B',\mathcal O)=B'$, $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)=B$ ([def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $\operatorname{Spec}\iota$ is the morphism corresponding to $\iota$ under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] for $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$). By the second clause of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], $\phi^{-1}(D(g))$ is the principal open of $\iota(g)=g$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, which we also write $D(g)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0) (with $X=U=\operatorname{Spec}B'$, resp. $X=U=\operatorname{Spec}B$), the restriction maps $B'\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B'}(D(g))$ and $B\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}(D(g))$ are localizations at $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], so we may identify these section rings with $B'_g$ and $B_g$.

source.place: Schemes Lemma Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine) with Tag 01HY (preimage of D(g)) and Lemma Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves: O(D(f))=R_f); used at more-algebra.tex:2546-2548

proof.text: The hypothesis says that $\phi$ restricts to an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$; in particular, for every open $W\subseteq U$ the sheaf map $\phi^\sharp_W:\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B'}(W)\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}(\phi^{-1}(W))$ is a ring isomorphism. Take $W=D(g)\subseteq U$ (step 3). The map $\phi^\sharp_{D(g)}$ commutes with the restrictions from global sections, and on global sections $\phi^\sharp$ is $\iota$ (step 4); so under the identifications of step 4, $\phi^\sharp_{D(g)}:B'_g\to B_g$ is a ring map whose composite with $B'\to B'_g$ is $B'\xrightarrow{\iota}B\to B_g$. Since every element of $B'_g$ is $b/g^n$, such a map is unique, hence it is the induced localization map $b/g^n\mapsto\iota(b)/g^n$. Therefore $B'_g\to B_g$ is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Split along more-algebra.tex:2542-2549 (proof of Stacks 09XH). Five steps: (1) a lift g_0 of the idempotent; Spec(C'_1)=V(IB'+(1-g_0)) is closed; (2) Z=Spec B' minus U is V(J), disjoint from V(K), so J+K=B' (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact (i)); (3) g=g_0 j lifts the idempotent and lies in J, so D(g) is in U (explicit construction written by the agent; Stacks only says 'this is possible'); (4) phi^{-1}(D(g))=D(g) and the sections over D(g) are B'_g, B_g (Mathlib leaves lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme, lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme (0)); (5) sections over D(g) of the isomorphism of locally ringed spaces over U give B'_g -> B_g bijective, identified with the localization map by its universal property (Stacks uses Algebra 00E9 'for example'; the statement's hypothesis makes the sections argument direct). No new nodes. Statement clarified: Spec(C'_1) in Spec(B'/IB') in Spec(B') via the surjections. stmt_deps kept as given (lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent, lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map, lem-weil-pbc-spec-integral-ring-map-integral are not used by the statement text). The hypotheses on B, C_1, C_2 are not used by the proof.

lean.statement: theorem integralClosure_finite_fibre_choose_g (A : Type v) (B : Type u) (C₁ : Type w₁) (C₂ : Type w₂) (C₁' : Type w₃) (C₂' : Type w₄) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C₁] [CommRing C₂] [CommRing C₁'] [CommRing C₂'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] (I : Ideal A) [Algebra (A ⧸ I) C₁] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) C₂] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) C₁'] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) C₂'] [Module.Finite (A ⧸ I) C₁] (eB : (B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) I) ≃+* C₁ × C₂) (eB' : (integralClosure A B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B)) I) ≃+* C₁' × C₂') (heB : ∀ a : A, eB (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A B a)) = algebraMap (A ⧸ I) (C₁ × C₂) (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a)) (heB' : ∀ a : A, eB' (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B) a)) = algebraMap (A ⧸ I) (C₁' × C₂') (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a)) (f₁ : C₁' →ₐ[A ⧸ I] C₁) (f₂ : C₂' →ₐ[A ⧸ I] C₂) (hprod : ∀ b : integralClosure A B, eB (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap (integralClosure A B) B b)) = (f₁ (eB' (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b)).1, f₂ (eB' (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b)).2)) (U : (Spec (.of (integralClosure A B))).Opens) (hU : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum C₁', (PrimeSpectrum.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk _) (PrimeSpectrum.comap ((RingHom.fst C₁' C₂').comp eB'.toRingHom) p) : PrimeSpectrum (integralClosure A B)) ∈ U) (hIso : IsIso (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (integralClosure A B) B)) ∣_ U)) : ∃ g : integralClosure A B, Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B)) I) g = eB'.symm (1, 0) ∧ (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (integralClosure A B), g ∉ (p.1 : Set (integralClosure A B)) → (p : Spec (.of (integralClosure A B))) ∈ U) ∧ Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap (integralClosure A B) B) g)
